lines.speaker: merc-thornwick-levyman
lines.line: That's a deep ford ahead, captain. My pike-contract stops at ankle-deep mud.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Two coppers are already in my palm. Keep your shaft dry and march.

lines.speaker: merc-thornwick-levyman
lines.line: Stay behind my kettle-helm when the gnolls rush the ditch, bowman.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Gladly. Just don't duck when my arrows pass an inch above your ear.

lines.speaker: merc-thornwick-levyman
lines.line: Any chance your cantrips can dry wet wool socks without setting them ablaze?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Keep marching, pikeman. Smoke gives away our position faster than squelching boots.

lines.speaker: merc-thornwick-levyman
lines.line: If I drop in these Border Fords, leave me in the peat. Don't make me walk twice.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Relax. Your debts stay with the Thornwick bailiff; your bones would serve me.

lines.speaker: merc-alder-poacher
lines.line: Your greaves clang louder than a tinker's cart. Every stag in Greywood hears us.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Let them hear. When they turn to look at my shield, you take the shot.

lines.speaker: merc-alder-poacher
lines.line: Your fletching's trimmed too wide for crosswinds off the Border Fords.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: And your bowstring's waxed with tallow. Worry about your own quiver, poacher.

lines.speaker: merc-alder-poacher
lines.line: That ozone smell on your sleeves ruins my downwind stalk every single morning.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Better ozone than gnoll fangs in your throat. Stay ten paces to my left.

lines.speaker: merc-alder-poacher
lines.line: Funny how corpses seem lighter on silver rings right after you check the brush.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Must be the swamp gas swelling their fingers, cap'n. Terribly tragic.

lines.speaker: merc-hedge-leech
lines.line: Stop squinting at my shoulder scar. The blade missed the joint.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: It missed by a fingernail, and whoever stitched it used twine fit for grain sacks.

lines.speaker: merc-hedge-leech
lines.line: Save me a handful of clean goose-quills. They make splendid drainage tubes.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Touch my arrows before a skirmish and you'll be testing those tubes on yourself.

lines.speaker: merc-hedge-leech
lines.line: Magic closes skin fast, sure, until the pus rots underneath. Leave the lancing to me.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Keep your mutton-fat salve away from my focus-crystal and we have a deal.

lines.speaker: merc-greywood-chopper
lines.line: This plank bridge looks spongy. Let me tap the pilings with my axe-poll first.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Make it quick. If raiders catch us mid-stream, wood rot will be our smallest worry.

lines.speaker: merc-greywood-chopper
lines.line: Give me three heartbeats to fell that dead alder across the ford—instant breastwork.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Save your swing. I'd rather have clear sightlines than splinter cover.

lines.speaker: merc-greywood-chopper
lines.line: When a pine falls, it stays down. Your corpses lack basic forest manners.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Dead wood burns; dead men carry shields. I prefer the latter.

lines.speaker: merc-lantern-novice
lines.line: Did you just singe your left eyebrow again? We haven't even seen a scout.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Static buildup in the fog! Totally normal. Just keep your oil-flasks behind me.

lines.speaker: merc-lantern-novice
lines.line: The hermit-prior claimed fire magic lacks subtlety. Clearly he never fought in knee-deep fen.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Subtlety keeps you alive when mana runs dry. Watch your fuel.

lines.speaker: merc-lantern-novice
lines.line: Oops—nearly scorched that corpse you were eyeing. Still usable?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Charred sinew snaps easily. Aim left next time or pay the burial fee.

lines.speaker: merc-parish-sexton
lines.line: Keep your knotted measuring cord away from my quiver while we're on watch.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Merely estimating coffin-timber for the Thornwick parish roll, bowman. Nothing personal.

lines.speaker: merc-parish-sexton
lines.line: Do you burn your dead in the academy, or leave them properly buried for collectors?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: We reduce them to clean ash so tomb-notaries don't come knocking.

lines.speaker: merc-parish-sexton
lines.line: Your technique is remarkably tidy—no wasted bone, no torn ligaments.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Learn the anatomy first, sexton. Shovels are only for beginners.

lines.speaker: merc-redmarsh-slinger
lines.line: Stop chewing that bitter alkali root—it makes you look like you're bleeding from the gums.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Keeps the spit flowing when the salt-wind dries your throat, iron-back.

lines.speaker: merc-redmarsh-slinger
lines.line: Bowstrings stretch in this dry glare. Lead shot never loses its draw-weight.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Until you run out of round pebbles. My arrows are reusable.

lines.speaker: merc-redmarsh-slinger
lines.line: Dune-corpses dry out like salted goat-meat. Hardly worth raising, wouldn't you say?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Dried sinew never rots in the heat, slinger. They march longer than you.

lines.speaker: merc-quarry-sapper
lines.line: Those sandstone ruins look solid enough for tonight's camp.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Sleep inside if you want a ceiling on your chest. I'll take the open scrub.

lines.speaker: merc-quarry-sapper
lines.line: My pick cracks the carapace; your bodkin slips into the soft meat underneath.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Simple arithmetic. Just don't block my lane when you swing.

lines.speaker: merc-quarry-sapper
lines.line: Gorrathul's overseers used ward-chains that burned skin on contact. Nasty work.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Iron breaks when heated and cooled fast. Remember that if we meet their slavers.

lines.speaker: merc-dune-houndmaster
lines.line: Three viper tracks crossing the salt-crust ahead. Tell your vanguard to watch their ankles.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Good eyes. Keep twenty paces ahead and signal before we crest the ridge.

lines.speaker: merc-dune-houndmaster
lines.line: You smell like dried lizard jerky. Are you carrying snacks in your quiver?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Keeps the fletching dry and feeds me on stakeouts. Want a strip?

lines.speaker: merc-dune-houndmaster
lines.line: Your dead don't breathe, which is handy in dust, though they walk like lame camels.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: They don't need grace to soak arrows meant for my scout.

lines.speaker: merc-cistern-acolyte
lines.line: My bow-limbs are warping in this furnace. Can your water-ward spare some mist?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Hold your yew near my staff at dusk. Not too close, or the hemp will slacken.

lines.speaker: merc-cistern-acolyte
lines.line: The hermitage said tapping a sacred cistern for melons was heresy. My melons fed three villages.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Practical magic always offends the elders. Keep the wards flowing.

lines.speaker: merc-cistern-acolyte
lines.line: Water brings life; your craft drinks the marrow dry. Strange company we keep.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Both preserve what the desert wants to erase, acolyte.

lines.speaker: merc-tomb-notary
lines.line: What's that papyrus strip dangling from your belt? A shopping list?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: An itemized tally of every brigand we've dispatched. Your vanguard owes me four entries.

lines.speaker: merc-tomb-notary
lines.line: That embalmer's hex on your left hand still pulses whenever we near tomb-ruins.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: A useful compass for old magic, though it aches terribly before rain.

lines.speaker: merc-tomb-notary
lines.line: Third-Dynasty liens hold surprisingly well in the Redmarsh dust.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Royal debt outlasts flesh and bone alike, notary. Serve the writ.

lines.speaker: merc-salt-mercenary
lines.line: You still sleep with that kite shield strapped to your forearm?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Habit from the Twin Passes. Waking up alive beats waking up comfortable.

lines.speaker: merc-salt-mercenary
lines.line: Tell me our quartermaster packed extra arrow-bundles before we crossed the flats.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Counted them myself at dawn. Nobody gets shorted while I'm watching.

lines.speaker: merc-salt-mercenary
lines.line: Redmarsh salt-crust eats iron shield-rims fast. Remember to oil yours tonight.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Already done. Worry about keeping sand out of your spell-components.

lines.speaker: merc-salt-mercenary
lines.line: At least your dead don't demand silver upfront before crossing a dune.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: No, though they complain far less than shield-sergeants.

lines.speaker: merc-hedge-leech
lines.line: Heatstroke kills faster than gnolls out here. Keep your juniper gin corked till dusk.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Medicinal dose only, mage! My suturing hand trembles worse in dry wind.

lines.speaker: merc-oakhaven-marine
lines.line: Tight stone alley ahead—just like a cutter's main deck in a boarding crush.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Good. Put shields in front and push until their backs hit the harbor wall.

lines.speaker: merc-oakhaven-marine
lines.line: Crosswinds off the cliffs gust twice per wave. Count three before releasing.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Already adjusted for the salt-drift, sailor. Watch your own footing.

lines.speaker: merc-oakhaven-marine
lines.line: Spitting over your left shoulder won't keep drowned sailors out of the surf.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Maybe not, necromancer, but it keeps my cutlass hand lucky.

lines.speaker: merc-harbor-arbalest
lines.line: Give me three seconds of shield-cover while I span the windlass.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: You'll have five. Just make sure that steel prod goes through their captain.

lines.speaker: merc-harbor-arbalest
lines.line: Longbows are fine for unarmored runners, but breastplates laugh at ash-shafts.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Only when you miss the visor-slit. Still, your bolts do make a satisfying clang.

lines.speaker: merc-harbor-arbalest
lines.line: If your lightning magnetizes my steel prods, they'll veer straight into the sea.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Keep ten paces clear of my arcs and your bolts will fly true.

lines.speaker: merc-storm-channeler
lines.line: My hair's standing straight up under my helm. Tell me you're not charging a bolt.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Just ambient squall-static! Though you might want to lower that iron spear.

lines.speaker: merc-storm-channeler
lines.line: Where did you even find rubberized boot-soles like those?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Borrowed from a retired lighthouse keeper. Best insulation on the Iron Coast.

lines.speaker: merc-storm-channeler
lines.line: Lightning chars flesh too badly for clean reanimation. Leave me a few intact.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: No promises when the tide rolls in and the armor gets wet.

lines.speaker: merc-triage-surgeon
lines.line: Stop staring at my collarbone every time we break camp, sawbones.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Magnificent symmetry, captain. Almost a shame to risk it on slippery sea-rocks.

lines.speaker: merc-triage-surgeon
lines.line: Salt-spray festers faster than swamp mud. Clean every graze with boiled vinegar.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Already carrying a flask. Just keep your specimen jars out of my pack.

lines.speaker: merc-triage-surgeon
lines.line: If you raise one of my fresh amputations, I expect half the salvage fee.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: You can keep the jars, surgeon. I only need the parts that still hold a spear.

lines.speaker: merc-drowned-arbiter
lines.line: Why refuse steamed mussels when the whole harbor reeks of fresh catch?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Shellfish feed on drowned men's memories, archer. I'll stick to dry biscuit.

lines.speaker: merc-drowned-arbiter
lines.line: Your brass wreck-bell resonates at an unsettling pitch whenever storm-clouds gather.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: It rings on the frequency of salt-bound oaths, mage. Listen and learn.

lines.speaker: merc-drowned-arbiter
lines.line: The drowned answer your bell faster than my own incantations raise the shore-dead.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: They owe unpaid passage to the tide, colleague. I merely call the roll.

lines.speaker: merc-ironclad-turncoat
lines.line: Still biting every crown before pocketing it? You'll chip a molar before dusk.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Old habit from Sundered Ranks. Clipped tin tastes awful, captain.

lines.speaker: merc-ironclad-turncoat
lines.line: Scavenged brigandine makes a racket on wet cobbles. Keep twenty paces back.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Quiet boots don't stop warhammers, archer. I'll take the heavy steel.

lines.speaker: merc-ironclad-turncoat
lines.line: You switched sides once when pay ran thin. What keeps you loyal here?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Prompt silver, dry rations, and a commander who doesn't waste men on vanity.

lines.speaker: merc-ironclad-turncoat
lines.line: If I catch a bolt on the seawall, make sure my pouch settles my tavern tab first.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: You'll live to spend it yourself, deserter. Keep your shield up.

lines.speaker: merc-greywood-chopper
lines.line: Driftwood along this coast burns blue with sea-salt—bad for signaling, great for warmth.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Hard as ironwood to split, too. Dulled two wedges before supper.

lines.speaker: merc-obsidian-sapper
lines.line: Keep your torch three paces back—prism-powder doesn't forgive stray sparks.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Sheathed and covered. Just crack that obsidian gate before the garrison rallies.

lines.speaker: merc-ironcamp-halberdier
lines.line: Hook their champion's shield-rim down and I'll put an arrow through his throat.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Just don't shoot while my haft is across his chest. Wait for the yank.

lines.speaker: merc-ironcamp-halberdier
lines.line: My eyebrows never grew back after Greystone. Keep your fire-bolts high when I engage.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Noted. Stay low and let the arcs pass overhead.

lines.speaker: merc-ironcamp-halberdier
lines.line: Ironcamp's wall-dead deserve rest, not another shift in the sulfur.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Only the Ember Court's servants rise today, halberdier. Your brothers rest.

lines.speaker: merc-slag-hound-sniper
lines.line: How do you see anything through those smoked-quartz goggles in this gloom?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Gloom doesn't blind you—magma-flare does. Keep your shield low.

lines.speaker: merc-obsidian-sapper
lines.line: Sulfur leak twenty paces left—smells like rotten eggs beneath the basalt crust.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Good nose, sapper. I'll keep fire-arrows out of my quiver till we pass.

lines.speaker: merc-slag-hound-sniper
lines.line: Redglass drake-splinters hold an edge better than forged steel in volcanic heat.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Careful—they also shatter violently if struck by frost-wards.

lines.speaker: merc-slag-hound-sniper
lines.line: A clean shot through the gorget leaves the rest of the corpse intact for you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Thoughtful as ever, marksman. Keep aiming high.

lines.speaker: merc-ash-battlemage
lines.line: Give the word when your frost locks their magma-plate, and I'll swing the mace.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Count two heartbeats after the steam bursts—that's when the iron turns brittle.

lines.speaker: merc-ash-battlemage
lines.line: Cold mist off your cuffs fogs my sightline every time we crest a sulfur ridge.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Step three paces upwind, archer, and you'll have crystal air.

lines.speaker: merc-obsidian-sapper
lines.line: Seven fingers are plenty to rig a blasting charge, provided you keep sparks off my belt.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: I'll stick to frost and wind until your quarrels are safely downrange.

lines.speaker: merc-ash-battlemage
lines.line: Flash-freezing flesh preserves every tendon. Your foundry craft suits my work.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Just keep your thralls clear when I shatter the ice-crust.

lines.speaker: merc-penitent-flagellant
lines.line: You march into cinder-storms without a visor. How do you read the enemy's swing?

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: By the hiss of displaced air and the weight of their boots on slag.

lines.speaker: merc-penitent-flagellant
lines.line: Your heartbeat sounds louder than a war-drum whenever we near the lava-vents.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: It keeps time for my penance, archer. Loose your arrows over my shoulder.

lines.speaker: merc-penitent-flagellant
lines.line: You blinded yourself with Ember Court ash, yet you walk straighter than men with two eyes.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Sight distracts the fearful, mage. Conviction needs no lantern.

lines.speaker: merc-obsidian-sapper
lines.line: Prism-powder turns siege-golems to gravel, though it leaves precious little for you to raise.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Better gravel than an intact golem crushing our frontline, demolitionist.

lines.speaker: merc-catacomb-bailiff
lines.line: Polishing those brass seal-weights again? We're marching into a siege, not a court.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Authority requires proper luster, captain. The First Watch respects neat protocol.

lines.speaker: merc-catacomb-bailiff
lines.line: Those spectral watchmen you summon never blink in volcanic ash.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: They served thirty years beneath the obsidian floor; a little cinder barely registers.

lines.speaker: merc-catacomb-bailiff
lines.line: Binding ancient oaths in hot wax takes remarkable control amid this ambient fire.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Archival discipline, mage. Panic is merely an unfiled form.

lines.speaker: merc-catacomb-bailiff
lines.line: Summoning the First Watch by docket number is far cleaner than raw blood-binding.

lines.speaker: player
lines.line: Every soldier deserves a proper discharge paper—even three centuries late.
